messages:
dennis: Quick question from a trip to Amsterdam 000 At a cafe the card terminal asked to charge in USD instead of EUR (DCC). I took the EUR receipt but my bank charged a higher amount because of DCC. Can I claim the DCC fee or should I ask vendors to charge in local currency?

clara: Good catch. Policy: always request to be charged in the local currency (EUR) to avoid dynamic currency conversion (DCC) markups. We do not reimburse the extra markup created by DCC when a merchant forces the conversion.

clara: If you unintentionally accepted DCC, upload both the merchant receipt showing local amount and the card statement showing the converted USD charge + a brief note explaining DCC was offered. Finance will try to reconcile but markups are generally non-reimbursable.

dennis: Ugh, the POS printed both lines: EUR 18.50 and USD 20.95 (card charged USD). I still have the paper receipt. Should I attach anything else?

manager-amy: Attach the receipt, card txn, and a photo of the terminal option if you have it (shows they offered DCC). If it's clear the merchant forced DCC (rare), we can escalate, but typically the traveler clicks the option so the extra is personal.

finance-bot: Reminder: expenses without clear supporting docs may be flagged. For currency issues, show original currency amounts and card conversion line.

clara: Also: foreign transaction fees from your bank (e.g., 1-3% FX fee) are reimbursable if incurred on a business-eligible card charge (not DCC markup). So differentiate bank FX fees vs merchant DCC markup in your note.

dennis: Helpful. Related Q: I paid for a taxi in cash in EUR and got a handwritten receipt. Can I also claim VAT back for that?

clara: VAT reclaim is tricky. For small cash receipts we generally don't process VAT refunds unless the vendor issues a VAT invoice with tax ID. For EU business travel, keep any VAT invoices with VAT registration info if you intend to reclaim VAT. Personal cash receipts without VAT id typically cannot be reclaimed.

clara: Short checklist:
```
- For DCC: always choose local currency. If DCC accepted accidentally: attach merchant receipt + card stmt + terminal photo/note.
- Bank FX fee: attach card stmt showing fee line; reimbursable.
- Merchant DCC markup: usually non-reimbursable unless merchant coerced you.
- VAT refunds: require VAT invoice with vendor tax ID; cash-only receipts usually not enough.
```

dennis: One more: I used a personal card and the bank added a cross-border fee (2.5%). Should I claim that on the expense?

manager-amy: Yes, if the underlying charge is business-eligible and you used a personal card because company card wasn't available, bank cross-border fees are reimbursable. Attach the card statement line showing the fee (labelled FX or foreign transaction fee) and note why personal card was used.

people-ops: Policy snippet: "Avoid DCC. Keep original currency receipts. Bank FX/cross-border fees are reimbursable when tied to business charges; merchant DCC markups are not reimbursable unless merchant error/coercion is proven."

dennis: Thanks all. I'll upload the paper receipt, card txn, terminal photo, and a quick note: "DCC offered, accepted accidentally; card charged USD 20.95 vs EUR 18.50"

clara: That will do. Finance may follow up but this matches prior cases. :thumbsup:
